recipes.name: Dark Chocolate and Avocado Mousse with Erythritol
recipes.description: An unctuous dessert where the fatty texture of ripe avocado replaces cream or butter, emulsified with pure fat-free cocoa and erythritol. It provides antioxidant polyphenols and monounsaturated lipids that do not alter the glucose curve.
instructions: Scoop the flesh of the ripe avocado into the blender cup or food processor.
Add the pure cocoa powder, erythritol, almond milk, vanilla extract, and the pinch of cinnamon.
Blend on high power for 2 continuous minutes, stopping to scrape the sides with a silicone spatula, until you get a silky, glossy mousse.
Divide the mousse between two individual glass cups.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before tasting so it takes body and a firm consistency.

recipes.name: Flourless Baked Rustic Ricotta and Lemon Tart
recipes.description: A fluffy, airy cake baked with low-fat ricotta, fresh eggs, and lemon zest, completely free of cookie bases or refined flours. It supplies high biological-value protein with a minimal percentage of net carbohydrates.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170 °C with top and bottom heat and line the base of an 18 cm round pan with parchment paper.
Separate the whites from the yolks of the three eggs into two clean bowls.
In the yolk bowl, add the drained ricotta, erythritol, lemon zest and juice, and vanilla; beat with whisk for 2 minutes until incorporated.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks with a pinch of salt in the other bowl.
Fold the beaten whites into the ricotta cream in three batches, using gentle sweeping motions from bottom to top with a spatula so as not to lose the air.
Pour the batter into the pan, smooth the surface, and bake at 170 °C for 35 minutes until golden and set in the center.
Let cool at room temperature, then refrigerate at least 2 hours before unmolding and dividing into 4 portions.

recipes.name: Light Vanilla Panna Cotta with Homemade Sugar-Free Raspberry Coulis
recipes.description: A traditional gelatin dessert made with almond plant milk and a moderate amount of mascarpone for dairy creaminess, topped with raspberries reduced over heat. The berries provide protective polyphenols without causing glycemic spikes.
instructions: Hydrate the unflavored gelatin sheets in a container of very cold water for 5 minutes.
In a saucepan, heat the almond milk with the mascarpone, half of the erythritol, and the vanilla over medium heat without letting it boil, stirring to dissolve the cheese.
Drain the gelatin sheets well by hand and add them to the hot saucepan, whisking until completely dissolved.
Pour the mixture into two glass cups and refrigerate for a minimum of 3 hours so it sets.
For the coulis, cook the raspberries in a small saucepan with the remaining erythritol and lemon juice for 4 minutes, mashing them with a fork; let cool.
Crown each set panna cotta cup with a spoonful of the cold raspberry coulis before serving.

recipes.name: Crunchy Almond Flour and Ceylon Cinnamon Cookies
recipes.description: Grain- and wheat-flour-free baked cookies made of finely ground almond, egg white, and aromatic cinnamon. They provide monounsaturated fatty acids and vitamin E with a residual carbohydrate content.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160 °C with top and bottom heat and prepare a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, mix the almond flour, erythritol, and ground cinnamon.
Add the egg white and vanilla extract, kneading with a spatula or your hands to form a compact, slightly sticky dough.
Divide the dough into 6 equal portions, form balls, and flatten them on the sheet with your palm until they are 5 mm thick.
Bake at 160 °C for 12 minutes until the edges take on a light golden tone.
Let cool completely on the sheet without touching them (they will harden and become crisp as the temperature drops). One serving is 2 cookies.

recipes.name: Pure Dark Chocolate Chia Pudding with Crunchy Nibs
recipes.description: A cold sweet gel formed by chia seeds hydrated in plant milk with 100% pure bitter cocoa and a non-caloric sweetener, crowned with bitter cacao nibs. Extremely rich in mucilaginous fiber that delays gastric emptying.
instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk the almond milk, cocoa powder, erythritol, and vanilla with hand whisk until the cocoa is dissolved with no lumps.
Add the chia seeds and mix vigorously for a full minute.
Let rest 10 minutes at room temperature and whisk again so the seeds do not settle at the bottom.
Divide the preparation between two individual glass cups or containers.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours (or overnight) until it sets into a pudding texture.
Sprinkle the crunchy pure bitter cacao nibs over the surface just before serving.

recipes.name: Fluffy Whole-Grain Oat, Plain Yogurt, and Orange Mini Cakes
recipes.description: Individual mini baked cakes made from ground whole-grain oat flakes, unsweetened strained yogurt, and fresh orange aroma. A clean source of satiating beta-glucans without a single gram of free sugars.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and prepare 3 individual silicone muffin or tartlet molds.
In a large bowl, beat the two eggs with the plain yogurt, erythritol, mild olive oil, and orange zest.
Add the sifted whole-grain oat flour and baking powder, mixing with a spatula until a uniform batter forms.
Distribute the mixture evenly among the 3 individual molds.
Bake at 180 °C for 16-18 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean and dry.
Let cool on a rack for 5 minutes before unmolding and serving warm or cold.

recipes.name: No-Churn Express Mixed Berry and Greek Yogurt Ice Cream
recipes.description: Instant creamy ice cream made by blending frozen mixed berries with thick Greek yogurt and erythritol in a processor. Quick, rich in probiotic bacteria and anthocyanin antioxidants with a very low glycemic load.
instructions: Place the frozen berries directly in the bowl of a food processor or powerful blender.
Add the plain Greek yogurt and powdered erythritol.
Process in pulses initially to break up the fruit, then blend continuously for 1 minute, stopping to scrape the ingredients down with a spatula, until you get a dense, uniform frozen cream.
Serve immediately with an ice cream scoop in two cold bowls.
Decorate with fresh mint leaves and eat right away to enjoy its creamy texture without ice crystals.

recipes.name: Oven-Baked Apples with Ceylon Cinnamon and Chopped Walnuts
recipes.description: Apples cooked in the gentle heat of the oven in their own juices with a cinnamon stick and a core filled with crunchy walnuts. The pectin gelled during baking forms a network that delays the absorption of the fruit's natural carbohydrates.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
Wash the apples and remove the core with a corer, taking care not to pierce the base of the fruit.
Make a shallow circular cut with the tip of the knife around the skin of each apple so they do not burst from the steam.
In a bowl, mix the chopped walnuts with the cinnamon and vanilla; fill the center cavity of both apples, pressing gently.
Place the apples in a small ovenproof dish and pour the 40 ml of water into the bottom of the sheet.
Bake at 190 °C for 25 minutes until the flesh is completely tender and caramelized.
Serve warm with their own roasting juices spooned over the top.

recipes.name: Homemade Bourbon Vanilla Egg Flan with Almond Milk
recipes.description: A lighter version of traditional flan that replaces condensed or sweetened milk with unsweetened plant milk and erythritol, gently set in a water bath. It offers choline and whole-egg protein with a very light calorie contribution.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160 °C and prepare a deep dish with 2 fingers of hot water for the water bath.
In a bowl, beat the 2 eggs with the erythritol and bourbon vanilla using a hand whisk until smooth without incorporating too much air.
Warm the almond milk slightly in the microwave or a saucepan (without boiling) and pour it in a thin stream over the beaten eggs while stirring continuously.
Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh strainer to remove bubbles and impurities and pour into two individual ceramic or glass flan molds.
Place the molds inside the water bath dish in the oven.
Bake at 160 °C for 25 minutes until the edges are firm and the center keeps a slight gelatinous wobble.
Remove from the oven, let cool at room temperature, and refrigerate at least 2 hours before unmolding or eating directly from the mold.

recipes.name: 85% Dark Chocolate, Almond, and Coconut Energy Truffles
recipes.description: No-bake dense bonbons made by melting very high-purity chocolate with almond flour and plant milk, coated in unsweetened desiccated coconut. They supply magnesium and healthy fats with under 4 g of net carbohydrates.
instructions: Chop the dark chocolate and melt it in a microwave-safe bowl in 30-second batches at medium power, stirring between each interval so it does not burn.
Add the almond milk, powdered erythritol, and almond flour to the melted chocolate; mix with a spoon until you get a compact, pasty dough.
Refrigerate the dough for 20 minutes so it firms up enough to shape.
Divide the dough into 6 equal portions and roll each between your palms to form rounded balls.
Roll the truffles over the shredded coconut laid out on a deep plate to cover them evenly.
Store in the fridge until consumed (one serving equals 2 truffles per person).

recipes.name: Warm Strawberry and Almond Flour Crumble
recipes.description: A low-carbohydrate version of the classic British dessert, where fresh strawberries cooked in their own juices are covered by a sandy, crunchy crust of ground almond and cinnamon. A delicious combination of textures with no free sugars.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
In two individual ceramic ovenproof dishes, distribute the chopped strawberries mixed with the lemon juice and half of the erythritol.
In a small bowl, prepare the crumble by mixing with your fingertips the almond flour, melted coconut oil, cinnamon, and the remaining erythritol until you get a loose crumb texture.
Distribute the crumble crumbs evenly over the strawberries without pressing down.
Bake at 180 °C for 16-18 minutes until the topping is golden and crunchy and the strawberry juices bubble at the edges.
Let cool 5 minutes and serve warm with a spoon.

recipes.name: Mini Cheesecake Cups with Cream Cheese and Blueberry Sauce
recipes.description: No-bake individual cups that combine a crunchy chopped-walnut base with a dense cream of white cheese beaten with lime, crowned by whole blueberries reduced over heat. Satisfying and rich in protective flavonoids.
instructions: Distribute the chopped walnuts in the bottom of two glass cups, pressing lightly with a teaspoon to form the base.
In a bowl, beat the cream cheese with the Greek yogurt, half of the erythritol, and the lime zest until you get a smooth, thick cream; pour over the walnut base.
In a small saucepan, heat the fresh blueberries with the lime juice and the remaining erythritol for 4 minutes over low heat, mashing some with a fork until you form a glossy sauce with whole chunks.
Let the blueberry sauce cool for 5 minutes.
Pour the blueberry sauce over the cheese cream in the cups.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour before eating well chilled.

recipes.name: Moist Carrot and Walnut Cake with Light Cheese Frosting
recipes.description: A moist carrot and walnut cake made with almond flour and erythritol, crowned with a light cream cheese frosting. A dessert with no added sugars.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175 °C with top and bottom heat and line a small rectangular pan with parchment paper.
Beat the two eggs with 40 g of the erythritol for 2 minutes until the mixture lightens slightly; add the plain Greek yogurt and vanilla.
Fold in the sifted almond flour, cinnamon, and baking powder, mixing with a spatula until you get a uniform, lump-free batter.
Add the grated carrot and 20 g of the chopped walnuts, integrating with folding motions; reserve the rest of the walnuts for decorating.
Pour the batter into the pan, smooth the surface, and bake at 175 °C for 28-30 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let cool completely on a rack; beat the cream cheese with the remaining 10 g of erythritol until you get a smooth frosting.
Spread the cheese frosting over the cold cake, sprinkle with the reserved walnuts, and divide into 4 portions.

recipes.name: Buckwheat Crêpes with Warm Sugar-Free Apple Compote
recipes.description: Thin crêpes made with pure buckwheat flour (whole-grain, gluten-free) filled with homemade apple compote flavored with clove and cinnamon. The fagomine present in buckwheat helps delay starch digestion.
instructions: In a small saucepan with 2 tablespoons of water, cook the apple cubes with the lemon juice and cinnamon over low heat for 8 minutes until tender; mash partially with a fork to form a chunky compote and keep warm.
In a bowl, whisk the buckwheat flour with the egg and the 100 ml of water until you get a smooth, liquid batter; let rest 3 minutes.
Grease a crêpe pan with a few drops of oil and heat over medium-high heat.
Pour half the batter, tilting the pan to spread it into a thin sheet; cook 2 minutes on one side and 1 minute on the other; repeat for the second crêpe.
Fill each crêpe with the warm apple compote.
Fold into triangles or cylinders and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Keto Brownie with 100% Pure Cocoa, Walnuts, and Almond Flour
recipes.description: A dense, chocolatey cake with a fudgy center, made with high-purity bitter cocoa, almond flour, and walnut chunks. It provides deep satisfaction for chocolate lovers with a negligible supply of simple sugars.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 170 °C and line a small square pan (15x15 cm) with baking paper.
In a bowl, mix the almond flour, pure cocoa powder, and erythritol.
Add the beaten eggs, melted coconut oil, and vanilla extract, incorporating with a spatula until you form a thick, chocolatey batter.
Fold in the chopped walnuts, distributing them through the batter.
Pour the mixture into the pan and smooth with the spatula.
Bake at 170 °C for 14-16 minutes (it is crucial not to overbake so the center keeps its dense moisture).
Let cool completely before unmolding and cutting into 3 rectangular portions.

recipes.name: Tiramisu-Style Cup with Mascarpone, Espresso, and Bitter Cocoa
recipes.description: An individual Italian-inspired cup that replaces sugared biscuits with a fluffy almond-flour base soaked in freshly brewed espresso, covered with an airy mascarpone cream and cocoa. Zero glucose spikes and intense flavor.
instructions: In a bowl, mix the almond flour with the hot espresso and 5 grams of erythritol to form a moist paste similar to a soaked biscuit.
Divide the almond-coffee mixture in the bottom of two glass cups.
In another bowl, beat the mascarpone with the remaining powdered erythritol and vanilla until you get an airy, consistent cream.
Arrange the mascarpone cream over the coffee base in both cups.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Dust the pure bitter cocoa through a fine strainer over the surface just before enjoying with a small spoon.

recipes.name: Star Anise and Cinnamon Poached Pears with Greek Yogurt
recipes.description: Pears gently cooked in an aromatic warm-spice infusion until tender and translucent, accompanied by a spoonful of creamy strained yogurt. The soluble fiber and yogurt cushion the release of the fruit's natural sugars.
instructions: In a narrow, deep saucepan, combine the water with the cinnamon stick, star anise, lemon zest, and erythritol; bring to a boil.
Peel the pears, keeping the top stem and trimming the base slightly so they stand upright.
Stand the pears upright in the saucepan with the boiling spice syrup.
Lower the heat to the minimum, cover, and cook for 18-20 minutes, turning carefully halfway through, until tender when pierced with a toothpick.
Transfer the pears to two deep dessert plates.
Accompany each pear with a portion of cold Greek yogurt on the side and drizzle with two tablespoons of the reduced aromatic cooking juice.

recipes.name: Fluffy Fresh Blueberry and Almond Flour Muffins
recipes.description: Fluffy individual baked bites made with pure almond flour, free-range eggs, and wild blueberries that burst during baking, adding moisture and freshness. Zero refined flours and controlled net carbohydrates.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and prepare 3 silicone muffin molds.
In a bowl, beat the two eggs with the erythritol, mild olive oil, and vanilla using a hand whisk.
Fold in the almond flour and baking powder, mixing with a spatula until you get a uniform batter.
Add the fresh blueberries and mix gently to distribute them without breaking them.
Divide the batter evenly among the 3 molds.
Bake at 180 °C for 16-18 minutes until they rise and turn golden on the surface.
Let cool on a rack before unmolding (1 muffin per serving).

recipes.name: Plain Yogurt, Mashed Raspberry, and Mint Popsicles
recipes.description: Refreshing popsicles made by alternating layers of unsweetened plain yogurt with rustic raspberry purée and chopped mint leaves. Ideal for hot weather, rich in probiotics and polyphenols with no added sugars.
instructions: In a bowl, mash the raspberries with the lemon juice, chopped mint, and half of the erythritol using a fork until you get a chunky rustic purée.
In another bowl, mix the plain yogurt with the remaining erythritol.
In two popsicle molds, alternately pour spoonfuls of the yogurt and raspberry purée to create a marbled effect.
Insert the wooden popsicle sticks in the center.
Freeze for a minimum of 4 hours until completely solid.
Run the mold under warm tap water for a few seconds to unmold easily and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Light Catalan Cream with Almond Milk and Burnt Cinnamon
recipes.description: An interpretation of the classic crema catalana that uses almond milk infused with cinnamon and lemon, set with yolks, and torched on the surface with a thin film of caramelized erythritol. Zero harmful burnt sugar.
instructions: Infuse the almond milk with the cinnamon and lemon zest over gentle heat for 5 minutes; strain.
Beat the 3 yolks with the 18 grams of erythritol until incorporated.
Pour the warm infused milk over the yolks without stopping stirring.
Cook over very gentle heat in a saucepan for 6-7 minutes, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until the cream thickens without boiling.
Divide the cream between two shallow clay or refractory ceramic dishes; let cool and refrigerate 2 hours.
Before serving, sprinkle the remaining 10 grams of erythritol in a thin layer over the surface and torch gently with a kitchen blowtorch until golden.

recipes.name: Frozen Pure Peanut Butter and Dark Chocolate Bonbons
recipes.description: Frozen bites with a creamy filling of single-ingredient peanut butter (no sugars or hydrogenated fats), bathed in a thin crisp shell of 85% cacao chocolate. High density of satisfying lipid energy with no net carbohydrates.
instructions: In a small bowl, mix the peanut butter with the powdered erythritol.
With a teaspoon, place 6 mounds of the peanut butter paste on a board covered with baking paper, forming 3 cm discs.
Place the board in the freezer for 20 minutes until the discs are completely frozen and firm.
Melt the dark chocolate with the coconut oil in the microwave in 20-second batches.
Take out the frozen peanut butter discs and dip them with the help of a fork into the melted chocolate (the chocolate will solidify almost instantly on contact with the cold).
Return to the freezer for 5 minutes and serve directly as a frozen bonbon (2 bonbons per person).

recipes.name: Warm Spiced Baked Pumpkin Tart with Nutmeg and Ginger
recipes.description: An autumnal warm tart inspired by American pumpkin pie that uses roasted pumpkin purée emulsified with eggs and pie spices, with no sweet pastry base. It provides beta-carotene and natural sweetness with prolonged digestibility.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175 °C and line an 18 cm round pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs with the erythritol until smooth.
Add the drained roasted pumpkin purée, almond milk, cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg; beat with a hand whisk until you form a smooth, lump-free cream.
Pour the mixture into the pan and smooth with a spatula.
Bake at 175 °C for 35 minutes until the surface is set and golden.
Let cool completely at room temperature (the texture will become firmer and creamier as it rests) and cut into 4 triangular portions.

recipes.name: Greek Yogurt, Sliced Strawberry, and Toasted Flax Parfait
recipes.description: An elegant parfait in a glass composed of alternating layers of protein-rich strained yogurt, thin slices of fresh strawberries, and toasted flax seeds that add crunch and omega-3 fatty acids. Visually tempting and very low in carbohydrates.
instructions: In a bowl, beat the Greek yogurt with the powdered erythritol and vanilla until you get a silky texture.
Wash, sanitize, and cut the strawberries into thin, even slices.
In two clear glass goblets, arrange a layer of sliced strawberries at the base.
Cover with a generous layer of beaten Greek yogurt.
Sprinkle a layer of crunchy toasted flax seeds.
Repeat the layers, finishing with strawberries and a touch of flax seeds on top before serving cold.

recipes.name: Light Baked Pure Cocoa Egg-White Soufflé
recipes.description: A warm, ethereal dessert that lifts egg whites beaten to stiff peaks with bitter cocoa and erythritol, baked in individual ramekins until they rise majestically. An ultra-light lean protein supply, flour-free, with virtually zero sugars.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C with top and bottom heat.
Brush the inside of two ceramic ramekins with the coconut oil using upward strokes (this helps the soufflé rise evenly) and dust the bottom with a pinch of cocoa.
In a clean, dry bowl, beat the 3 egg whites to stiff peaks with the lemon juice using an electric whisk.
Add the powdered erythritol gradually while continuing to beat to form a firm, glossy meringue.
Sift the pure cocoa powder over the meringue and fold it in with very gentle spatula motions so as not to deflate the air volume.
Divide the batter between the two ramekins, smoothing the surface with a spatula and running your fingertip around the inner rim to loosen the batter.
Bake at 190 °C for 10-12 minutes without opening the oven until they have risen above the rim.
Serve immediately at the table before they lose height.

recipes.name: No-Bake Cold Coconut and Lime Tart with Almond Crust
recipes.description: A refreshing Caribbean-style no-bake tart: a compacted toasted almond base with a silky filling set with coconut milk, fresh lime juice, and zest. A gastronomic finish full of citrus flavor, healthy fats, and no glycemic disruption.
instructions: In a bowl, mix the almond flour with the melted coconut oil and 10 grams of erythritol to form a wet-sand texture.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of a small springform pan (16 cm) lined with parchment paper to create a compact base; refrigerate while you make the filling.
Hydrate the gelatin sheets in very cold water for 5 minutes.
In a saucepan, heat the coconut milk with the remaining erythritol, lime juice, and half of the lime zest over medium heat without letting it boil.
Drain the gelatin by hand, add it to the hot saucepan, and stir with a whisk until completely dissolved.
Pour the liquid coconut-lime filling over the cold almond base in the pan.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours until completely set and firm.
Unmold carefully, decorate the surface with the remaining fresh lime zest, and cut into 4 triangular portions to serve.
